The fog had been rolling in off the North Sea for three days, thick enough to taste like salt and iron. Elias Thorne, the lighthouse keeper of Blackrock Point, had grown accustomed to the isolation, but the silence of the storm was different. It wasn’t the roaring of wind or the crash of waves; it was a low, rhythmic hum that seemed to vibrate in his teeth.

Elias adjusted the Fresnel lens, his oil-stained hands trembling slightly. The beam swept across the churning black water, illuminating nothing but the void. He checked the logbook, noting the barometric pressure dropping. Then, he heard it again. *Thump. Thump. Thump.*

It wasn’t coming from the sea. It was coming from the basement, from the old, sealed-off service tunnel that led to the cliff face.

Elias grabbed his lantern and descended the spiral stairs. The air grew colder, carrying the scent of wet stone and something else—something metallic and ancient. At the bottom of the tunnel, a rusted iron door stood ajar. He pushed it open.
